rationale: Canonical Typed Event vs Side Channel -> unknown/unknown: A taxonomy is an institution in Ostrom's sense — a shared resource governed by rules-in-use. Side channels are tragedy-of-the-commons moves: each one is locally cheap, and each one degrades the institutional value of the taxonomy. Once the taxonomy is no longer a complete description of what flows, it stops being trusted as a contract; once it stops being a contract, every new consumer must discover what flows empirically; once that becomes normal, the taxonomy is dead documentation and the wire is a free-for-all. Typed events have non-obvious downstream value: replay tooling can deterministically rebuild state from the event log; new consumers can subscribe without coordination; backpressure and prioritisation can be implemented uniformly. Every side channel forecloses on these capabilities for the data it carries. The pattern also closes a peripheral-design loop. Heartbeat (peripherals/progress-heartbeat-distinct-from-cycle-completion) is exactly the case: the watchdog needs a liveness signal distinct from cycle events. The wrong move is a separate ping mechanism. The right move is to add a "heartbeat" typed event to the same transport, so watchdogs subscribe to the same wire as everything else. The pattern is also the principled defence against the "lightweight" euphemism (feedback_lightweight_euphemism, agent memory): a "lightweight side channel" is the precise shape of work that appears done but isn't institutionalised. Translation: it is a typed event missing its taxonomy entry.

rationale: Constrained Execution Envelope -> unknown/unknown: Forbidding distracting actions does not work. A prohibition is a negative statement that requires the agent to hold both the forbidden action and the reason for forbidding it in mind — which is itself a distraction. It is a known pattern from philosophy (Nietzsche's critique of negation, Spinoza's "omnis determinatio est negatio" read in reverse) that productive constraint works by affirming what is present, not by denying what is absent. You do not teach someone to play chess by listing the moves they cannot make; you teach them the moves they can make, and the board enforces the rest. Even apparently negative concepts (Hegelian synthesis, apophatic theology, boundary conditions in mathematics) function as positive statements when they are operative: a synthesis is a new thing, not the absence of two old things; a boundary condition is a value the solution must take, not a region it must avoid. The peripheral is the positive statement. It says: here is what you can do, here is the sequence, here is when you are done. The agent inhabits this envelope and does the work. The constraint is not felt as restriction but as structure — the way a sonnet form is not a restriction on poetry but a structure that produces it.

rationale: Inhabitation Feeds Evolution -> unknown/unknown: The symmetry between agents and humans reveals the pattern. When Claude bypasses the proof peripheral to one-shot tool calls, and when Joe bypasses the REPL to type in a terminal, they are both starving the same learning loop for the same reason: the primitive path has less friction. The consequence is the same in both cases: no structured data is generated, no evidence accumulates, no peripheral evolution is possible, and the gap between the primitive path and the infrastructure path never closes. The Baldwin effect is subtle because it requires seeing the peripheral as a representational space, not just a constraint. A constraint that is not inhabited is merely a rule. A representational space that is inhabited is a learning engine. The difference is whether the peripheral generates data that feeds back into its own design. This is why surface usability is not cosmetic. It is the entry condition for the Baldwin loop. A peripheral with perfect design but poor surface is like a genotype with perfect fitness in a niche that the organism never enters: theoretically optimal, actually inert.

rationale: Pattern Becomes Peripheral -> jelo/生: The absorbed-input mode reveals why this matters. In the absorbed case, an individual gains something — skills, experience, CV lines, working code — but the system gains nothing. The trainer leaves and takes the knowledge with them. The agent writes code but no institutional learning accumulates. The developer uses Stack Overflow and gets a working function but no understanding of why it works. What doesn't happen in the absorbed case is the creation of new institutions (Ostrom). The trainer doesn't create a community of practice at their institution. The agent doesn't produce evidence that improves the proof peripheral. The developer doesn't contribute a pattern back to the library. The individual transacts with the system but the system does not change. This is the "programming by Stack Exchange" failure mode applied universally. An interaction that produces output without producing capability is an interaction that has been *absorbed* rather than *institutionalised*. The output is real — the code works, the training was delivered, the problem was solved — but it is non-generative. Nothing was learned at the system level. No new institution was created. No peripheral evolved. The pattern-to-peripheral bridge is what converts absorbed input into institutional creation. When a pattern becomes a peripheral: 1. The envelope defines a positive action space (not a prohibition). 2. The surface earns entry (not commands it). 3. Inhabitation generates data (not just output). 4. The data feeds back into the peripheral's design (Baldwin loop). 5. The improved peripheral earns further inhabitation (virtuous cycle). At step 5, something new exists that didn't exist before: an institution in Ostrom's sense — a set of rules-in-use that govern a shared resource (the action space) and that evolve through the participation of their inhabitants. This is what the absorbed-input mode fails to produce, and it is what the pattern-to-peripheral transition is for. The Spinozan frame is the deepest one: the question is not "did the agent obey the pattern?" but "did the agent's power to act increase?" If it did, the pattern has become a peripheral. If it didn't — if the agent merely transacted and moved on — the pattern remains documentation, however correct it may be.

rationale: Pilot Plus Ground Control -> unknown/unknown: The envelope boundary is exactly where the two kinds of integrity live. rationale: Progress Heartbeat Distinct From Cycle Completion -> unknown/unknown: The problem is fundamentally one of clock alignment. Cycle phase runs on a work-bounded clock (this cycle takes as long as the work takes). Liveness needs to run on a wall-clock or a tick-clock (silence is measured in seconds since something happened). Trying to use one clock for both produces the FM-regulator-vs-watchdog confusion: the regulator wants long cycles for big work; the watchdog wants short cycles for fast detection; they cannot both win on the same axis. The fix — separate channels for separate clocks — is the same pattern as feedback_perceived_time_dual_clock (agent memory): two clocks must be bridged through an explicit convolution, not papered over by treating one as the other. Heartbeats and cycle events are two clocks; the convolution is the watchdog's silence calculation. The pattern has an institutional reading too: peripheral cycles are glacial-loop events (M-cycle, M-mission, M-cycle-of-cycles). Progress heartbeats are social-loop events (something just happened). The distinction is the same as inhabitation-feeds-evolution's fast/slow split, applied to the liveness question.

rationale: Read-Only First, Then Extend -> unknown/unknown: The escalation matches the natural epistemic order. To know what writes should look like, you need to observe what is being read and where the gaps are. To know what consent should feel like, you need to have made some writes and noticed the friction. To know what envelope is safe, you need to have made consent-gated writes long enough to see the failure modes. Skipping stages means designing later stages on speculation rather than observation. Speculative design is exactly what the peripheral framing is meant to displace. The pattern also matches the consent-gate-as-locus-of-WM-I4 principle: the consent step is a first-class artefact, and the migration from supervised to autonomous is the swap of operator- consent for autopen-consent at a single, documented location. That swap is only safe after the operator has spent enough time consenting to know what they are signing off on. The Pair stage is where that knowledge accumulates. Crucially, "read-only first" is not the same as "don't ship anything until you understand everything." Observer is a real shipped peripheral — it has inhabitation, it produces value (the display is used), it generates Baldwin-loop data. It is just a peripheral whose capability is exactly read, no more.

rationale: Split Transport From Embodiment -> unknown/unknown: The stack already pays for this split implicitly everywhere it works: drawbridge separates message routing from agent representation; the War Machine separates the AIF engine from the markdown/web UI renderers; the REPL separates the chat protocol from the posframe surface. Where peripherals fail to be portable or composable, it is almost always because the split was elided at design time. The deeper reason is that transport and embodiment evolve at different timescales. Transport schemas are slow-changing institutional artefacts (changing them breaks every consumer). Embodiments are fast-changing UX artefacts (a posframe today, an overlay tomorrow). When the two are fused, the embodiment's fast-changing nature contaminates the transport — and the transport's institutional weight ossifies the embodiment. This split is also what makes peripherals composable. Two peripherals that share a transport layer can coordinate (cursor presence + selection presence both ride the same "editor presence" event stream). Two peripherals that share an embodiment surface can cooperate (a statusline that shows both build status and presence count). Without the split, every peripheral is a silo.
